ACTION 24 OF 32 · PHASE 06

Add a simple CRM or dashboard only when needed

Keep leads, bookings and follow-ups organized without buying or building an unnecessarily large system.

WHEN TO DO THISAfter real inquiries/orders reveal a recurring tracking problem.ESTIMATED WORK TIME2–6 hours for a small design; implementation varies
↗
Your one job

Keep leads, bookings and follow-ups organized without buying or building an unnecessarily large system.

01

Do this now

  1. 01

    Start with a simple table: contact, enquiry source, status, owner, quote, next follow-up, outcome and date.

  2. 02

    Define a small status flow such as NEW → CONTACTED → QUOTED → BOOKED / LOST.

  3. 03

    If a spreadsheet becomes a bottleneck, build a minimal admin dashboard with role-based login and only the fields users need.

  4. 04

    Add automation last: reminders, missed-lead alerts and reports; test permissions and customer consent.

02

Copy this into ChatGPT

Replace anything in [square brackets] with your real business details. The prompt is a shortcut, not a substitute for the steps above.

READY-TO-USE PROMPT
Design the smallest useful CRM for [BUSINESS]. Start with the manual process and fields, then provide a database schema, status transitions, admin roles, views and follow-up alerts only if needed. Account for privacy, permission checks, backups and mobile usability. Separate MVP from nice-to-have features and define a test for each critical workflow.
03

Finish with this

A lead pipeline with one owner and a measured follow-up process.

Before moving on, check your work against the following:

  • Leads can be updated from first inquiry to outcome
  • An owner is accountable for follow-ups
  • Admin access is not public
DON’T MAKE THIS MISTAKE

Building a giant CRM before finding out how customers actually book.

READY TO MOVE ON?

A real customer completes a verified lead or checkout flow; admin access and customer data are protected.
